meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (French/Belgian tradition, codified commercial law; unitary national jurisdiction, no sub-state tax differentiation)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: EU Internal Market Treaties (freedom of establishment and free movement of capital)
BLEU (Belgium-Luxembourg Economic Union) BIT network of 80+ bilateral investment treaties
US-Luxembourg Treaty of Friendship, Establishment and Navigation (1962)
OECD/UN Model-based DTA network of approximately 85 double tax agreements

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing (as amended, including AMLD5 transpositions of 25 March 2020); Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE / Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs) (as amended 2020); Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies (SCSp provisions inserted by Law of 23 July 2016); CSSF and professional body circulars on KYC/CDD.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent national civil registry or police authority of the shareholder's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille pursuant to the Hague Convention of 5 October 1961 (consular legalization only for non-contracting states)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address (utility bill or municipal certificate) of each UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Local utility provider or municipal registry in country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or consular legalization for non-Hague states)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized source-of-wealth and source-of-funds declaration executed by each UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary in the UBO's country of residence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing (corporate shareholders only)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Applicable companies register in the corporate shareholder's jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or consular legalization where the issuing state is not an Apostille member)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Reference letter from the introducing bank or licensed financial institution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commercial bank of the shareholder or UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or authenticated signature confirmation by the issuing bank's compliance officer

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory AML/CFT due diligence under the Law of 12 November 2004: identification and verification of all UBOs; enhanced due diligence for politically exposed persons (PEP per FATF/AMLD5 domestic and foreign categories), including beneficial ownership and source-of-funds analysis; mandatory screening against EU consolidated financial sanctions lists, UN Security Council consolidated sanctions, EU terrorist lists (CFSP), CSSF supervisory notices, and OFAC sanctions lists (restricted content), plus negative media check and adverse press review; all findings to be documented in an AML file for civil liability limitations. The operating SCSp sits in a Low_Risk_Standard AML tier; however the formation notary, RBE filing agent, and any credit institution or payment processor (Swift/Wire and Stripe as planned rails) will impose current-period sanctions screening at onboarding and on a rolling basis.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), official portal at www.lbr.lu; electronic filing via the RCS e-registration interface (eGrille) reachable through guichet.public.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: All filings must be drafted in French as the primary administrative language; company names may be expressed in any language provable in Latin alphabet script, and non-Latin scripts require verified transliteration (romanization) into Latin characters; the chosen name must linguistically comply with the legal form designation requirement, i.e. must contain 'Société en Commandite Spéciale' or the abbreviation 'SCSp'; names must be distinguishable (non-confusing) from all existing registered names, trade names, and protected intellectual property notations held in the RCS database.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: BANK (requires prior CSSF banking licensing authorization)
SICAV / SICAF / SIF / SICAR / RAIF / FCP (requires CSSF supervised investment fund authorization)
LUXEMBOURG / LUXEMBURG (requires ministerial authorization under the Law of 23 June 2006 on the protection of national designations)
ETAT / ADMINISTRATION / COMMUNE / ROYAL / GOVERNMENTAL (public authority terms requiring special dispensation)
S.A. / S.À R.L. / S.E. / SCA / SCS (legal form abbreviations inconsistent with an SCSp designation)
Terms contrary to public order, good morals, or objective public law
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the RCS/LBR refuses a name reservation (by reasoned decision), the applicant may re-file a revised reservation request through the LBR portal after removing the conflicting term. In parallel, formal appeals against a refusal are lodged by way of a petition before the Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg (commercial chamber) within one (1) month of notification of the refusal. Alternatively, if the refusal is based on a third-party trademark opposition, the applicant may submit a negotiation letter or brand authorization from the rights holder. No administrative extension of the 90-day reservation period is available; upon expiration the name is automatically released and the applicant must re-file a new reservation request through the LBR e-form (official fee re-applies).

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible in principle for a non-licensed IT services partnership: the SCSp must hold a registered office (siège social) located in Luxembourg, which an authorized domiciliation entity may provide as a shared 'registered office address' service including mail forwarding and legal correspondence handling. A virtual office is acceptable for RCS and UBO register compliance, but economic-substance documentation and tax-residence analysis under Luxembourg administrative practice (Loi du 10 août 1915, article 100-1) require the SCSp to be able to evidence if challenged; for this software-development and middleware licensing business, a virtual office without physical premises is acceptable only if combined with at least one Luxembourg-resident general partner (or managing partner agent) and the maintenance of local books and general-partner decision-making records.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low risk, quantified at below 5% probability per entity-year for a Low_Risk_Standard non-licensed technology partnership not holding real estate or regulated financial assets; an unannounced on-site inspection could nevertheless occur as part of RCS verification, CSSF on-boardings related to the intended payment/credit lines, or criminal/AML inquiries. Maintaining a central administration address in Luxembourg with correct RCS signage and complete partnership minute books reduces inspection triggers.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (including the provisions on société en commandite spéciale introduced by the Law of 12 July 2013), specifically the articles governing partnership formations and registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés – RCSL), operated by the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR), Département des sociétés.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Partnership Agreement (Contrat de Société) and application for registration (Demande d'inscription au RCSL).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is required by law for an SCSp; there is no statutory escrow account requirement. Contributions may be made in cash or in kind as agreed in the Partnership Agreement, and a bank confirmation letter is customarily presented for RCSL filing if capital is funded.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: The initial limited partner subscribes to one partnership interest at the contribution stated in the Partnership Agreement, which the General Partner accepts. RESOLVED: The registered office of the Partnership is fixed at [street address], L-[postal code], Luxembourg. RESOLVED: [Name] is appointed General Partner and [Name] is appointed Manager, each with sole signatory powers. RESOLVED: The General Partner is authorised to sign all filings with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register, tax, social security and municipal authorities and to take all ancillary steps to incorporate the Partnership.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and execution of the Partnership Agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg civil-law notary (recommended) or all partners by private deed, in accordance with the Law of 10 August 1915
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Partnership Agreement including corporate name, registered office address, general partner, limited partners, profit-sharing ratio, management and representation clauses, and contribution schedule. Arrange execution before a notary if drafting is notarised, or execute by private written instrument with verifiable electronic signatures. Ensure AML/KYC files and ultimate beneficial owner forms are prepared.
required_dossiers: Passport or national ID of the general partner and initial limited partner
AML/KYC questionnaire and beneficial ownership declaration
Power of attorney if a third party signs
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the competent authority queries the deed, amend the deficient clauses by addendum or re-execute before the notary. Consequential administrative corrections are made before filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: RCSL/Luxembourg Business Registers via online platform www.lbr.lu
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the proposed SCSp name to the LBR online name-search/reservation module. Confirm that the name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered legal entity or protected trademark. Reserve the name for a maximum of three months if accepted.
required_dossiers: Copy of the requesting partner's passport or ID
Extract of any conflicting trademark or entity if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, propose up to three alternative names through the same portal and, where necessary, request administrative review by the RCSL naming committee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank account opening and contribution verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution authorised by the CSSF (Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a partnership account in the name of the SCSp or a blocked pre-formation account. Deposit the agreed initial contribution, which may be zero or a token amount. Obtain a capital/asset confirmation letter or account opening certificate verifying the contribution for submission with the RCSL registration file.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests further due diligence, provide notarised bank statements, audited source-of-wealth documentation, or a legal opinion confirming the identity of the ultimate beneficial owner.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RCSL registration and formal incorporation filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCSL) – Département des sociétés
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the e-registration application through the LBR online portal or at the RCSL desk. Attach the notarised or private Partnership Agreement, identification documents of the general partner, bank attestation, and notifications required under Regulation 2018/1433. Upon approval, the RCSL assigns the RCS registration number and publishes the filing in the Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations (RESA).
required_dossiers: Completed RCSL application form signed by the general partner
Original or certified copy of the Partnership Agreement
Proof of identity of the general partner and managers
Legal entity extract if a corporate partner is involved
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond in writing to RCSL queries within fifteen calendar days; file a rectification memorandum or revise the Partnership Agreement if needed. Re-submission is made with a corrective note without re-notarisation if the amendment is administrative.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, VAT and social security registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD); Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the RCS registration number, obtain the Luxembourg business identification number from the ACD. Register for VAT through the AEDT if the partnership supplies cross-border digital services or expects to exceed VAT thresholds (which are generally mandatorily aligned with EU rules for digital B2B services). Register any employees with the CCSS and file employer declarations.
required_dossiers: RCS registration extract with RCS number
Identity details of the general partner and managers
Social security form for any employees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the ACD requests clarification on UBO or governing law, submit an organisation chart and legal opinion. For VAT registration, the taxpayer may file an explanatory statement with AEDT and apply for an administrative review within thirty days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal declaration and ancillary licensing verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commune (Municipality) of the registered office; Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM) for workplace safety
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Verify under the Luxembourg Law of 19 December 2014 on commercial permits whether any establishment permit is required for the intended software-development and anti-cheat middleware activity; generally, no such permit applies to ISIC 6201. File a municipal occupation declaration for business tax and, if applicable, a fire-safety conformity certificate for the premises.
required_dossiers: Lease agreement or proof of registered office
Fire-safety certificate if required by communal regulations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipality classifies the activity as requiring a classified-installation authorisation, submit the appropriate application under the Grand-Ducal regulation on classified establishments and, if misclassified, appeal to the municipal council within one month.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable – Ministry of the Economy, Directorate General for Industry, does not licence pure-software or middleware development activities. If physical manufacturing were later added, the relevant authority would be the Ministry of the Economy's Industrial Department.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No statutory operational licence required for a video-game anti-cheat middleware engine under Luxembourg or EU law; no commercial establishment permit applies under the Law of 19 December 2014 to ISIC 6201 software engineering activities.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'Environnement (Luxembourg Environmental Protection Administration) within the Ministry of the Environment, Climate and Sustainable Development
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from full EIA and from environmental registration – office-based software development is not a listed classified installation under the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 15 July 2018 on classified establishments.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater, VOC, or combustion emissions arise from normal software-development operations. The partnership must nevertheless comply with the EU Waste Framework Directive (2008/98/EC), the Luxembourg Law of 21 March 2012 on waste management, and WEEE recycling requirements for IT hardware. If emergency diesel generators or large server-room cooling units are installed, exhaust-gas emission thresholds under the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 15 December 1995 apply.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire-safety certification (attestation de sécurité incendie) is required from the municipal fire-safety authority for any office or server-room premises. Structural load inspection is necessary only if heavy cooling or server racks are installed. Occupational health clearance from the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM) is required for workstations, electrical installations, and ergonomic compliance.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) – Luxembourg Direct Tax Administration (33, rue de Gasperich, L-5826 Hesperange) for corporate income tax, municipal business tax and net wealth tax; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) – VAT and Registration Administration (1-3, avenue Guillaume, L-1651 Luxembourg) for VAT and registration duties. Official e-portals: MyGuichet.lu and guichet.lu; eTVA (VAT returns), eCDF (direct tax filings); legal gazette: legilux.public.lu.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: (1) Prepare the SCSp partnership deed (contrat de société, no notarial form mandatory) and register the entity with the Trade and Companies Register (RCS/Luxembourg Business Registers), which automatically issues the 13-digit national business identification number (matricule / numéro national) serving as the income-tax reference; (2) file the AEDT VAT registration (form 640 'demande d'immatriculation à la TVA') electronically via MyGuichet – the AEDT issues an LU-prefixed 8-digit VAT number (format LU12345678), generally within 7 working days; (3) open the direct-tax file at the ACD using the transparency return (déclaration commune under Article 175 LIR) where the SCSp itself files once naming all partners; (4) register all partners, including foreign general partners and corporate limited partners, via the RCS/ACD matricule system; no payroll registration applies in the absence of Luxembourg employees.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible – the SCSp (Société en Commandite Spéciale), created by the Law of 23 July 2016, lacks legal personality and is fiscally transparent by operation of law: no Luxembourg corporate income tax (IRC), no municipal business tax (ICC), and no net wealth tax (IFL) at SCSp level; profits, gains and net wealth are allocated directly to partners, who are taxable in their own Member State/residence; non-resident partners have no Luxembourg tax exposure absent a Luxembourg permanent establishment or Luxembourg real estate. No Luxembourg withholding tax is levied on partnership distributions. For the gaming anti-cheat middleware licensing activity (ISIC 6201/NAICS 541511) conducted without any Luxembourg PE, no CIT return is due at entity level.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg does not provide a domestic 'check-the-box' regime; SCSp transparency is statutory and may not be overridden in Luxembourg. Available mechanisms: (1) an SCSp may elect, under Article 175 LIR, to file a single consolidated transparency return naming all partners instead of per-partner filing; (2) US partners may file US Form 8832 to elect partnership or association classification – flanked by Luxembourg's ATAD hybrid-mismatch rules (Law of 21 December 2018) which deny deductions or impose inclusion where the SCSp is treated as an opaque entity abroad; (3) DAC6 (Law of 25 March 2020) mandates disclosure of reportable cross-border arrangements exploiting SCSp hybrid status; (4) treaty classification follows the OECD transparent-entity clause (no election available for double-tax-treaty qualification).

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT – Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée (TVA), implemented by the Luxembourg VAT Law of 12 February 1979 (Loi TVA), as amended, transposing EU Directive 2006/112/EC, including the 2021 e-commerce reform (Union/Non-Union OSS and IOSS).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 – annual taxable turnover (excl. VAT) threshold for the small-business VAT franchise exemption (Article 57 Loi TVA, in force from 1 January 2024; formerly EUR 30,000); VAT registration is compulsory above EUR 35,000. B2B supplies of anti-cheat middleware to Luxembourg or other EU business customers fall under the reverse-charge mechanism (no local registration needed for the non-resident supplier). For B2C e-services: EU-established suppliers apply a EUR 10,000 EU-wide distance/e-services threshold; non-EU suppliers of B2C e-services may sign up to the Union/Non-Union OSS and need no Luxembourg fixed establishment.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction controls or digital stamping regime exists in Luxembourg; there is no API pre-authorisation of invoices by the AEDT. E-invoicing is voluntary for B2B transactions. Compulsory e-invoicing applies only to B2G: invoices to central-government entities must be submitted as EN 16931 structured e-invoices (PEPPOL BIS 3.0) via a PEPPOL access point/MyGuichet gateway under the Law of 22 May 2019 (mandatory for central state bodies since 1 July 2022). Postponed EU VAT-in-the-Digital-Age (ViDA) measures will later introduce standardised B2B e-invoicing and continuous transaction controls (target implementation after 2030).

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: (A) Goods: 0% export exemption (Article 24 Loi TVA implementing Article 146 Directive 2006/112/EC) applies where the seller dispatches goods outside the EU within 90 days of supply and retains the export declaration and transport evidence. (B) Software/middleware provided as downloadable licences or cloud services: zero-rating follows the place-of-supply rules – B2B electronic services are outside Luxembourg VAT and subject to reverse charge at the customer's establishment (Article 14 Loi TVA); B2C e-services of non-established suppliers are taxed in the customer's Member State via OSS (Article 16 Loi TVA; Articles 58/59 Directive). For non-EU customers (arm's-length OEM game studios), the supply is outside the scope of Luxembourg VAT and no local VAT is chargeable; invoices must state that the place of supply is outside the EU and, for EU customers, 'reverse charge' with the customer's VAT ID.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Electronic customs export declaration (SAD/export Entry with MRN) evidencing exit of tangible media or hardware dongles from the EU, or the signed licence/service agreement for pure e-delivery as substitute export evidence
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / CMR (multimodal transport document) proving dispatch within the 90-day export period where physical goods are involved

Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) – bank credit advice / SWIFT MT103 evidencing payment in the agreed currency, issued by the receiving Luxembourg credit institution (original statement, not photostatic copy)
Commercial invoice, purchase order, order acceptance and licence deployment schedule reconciled to the payment rail (SWIFT Wire or Stripe)
EU/non-EU customer identity documentation (VIES VAT validation result for EU customers; certificate of incorporation or tax-residence certificate for non-EU customers)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: AEDT/ACD risk-based audits and cross-border information exchanges (DAC7, EU VAT exchange) examine export documentation in substance-over-form reviews. If zero-rating is unsupported or documentation is fabricated, the AEDT reverses the 0% treatment and assesses VAT at 17% on the full consideration, plus late-payment interest of 0.6% per month from the original return due date. Statute of limitations: five years for ordinary assessments, extended to ten years in fraud cases. Civil and criminal sanctions under Articles 426–433 LGI: administrative fines up to EUR 1,500 per infringement; criminal fines up to EUR 250,000 and imprisonment up to five years for fraudulent export claims, with publication of the conviction and joint and several liability of the general partner (commandité). Luxembourg statute does not impose a fixed 180-day FX repatriation deadline; the 180-day parameter is the ACD's customary documentary benchmark, and un-repatriated receivables beyond that period may be re-characterised as constructive distributions to the partner in an audit.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) as central bank within the Eurosystem, with the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) exercising day-to-day prudential and AML/CFT supervision over credit institutions and payment institutions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg maintains full current-account and capital-account convertibility. Article 63 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU) guarantees unrestricted movement of capital and payments within and into the EU; no local exchange-control legislation imposes approval, quota, or repatriation limits. Eurozone membership confers exchange-rate certainty within the single currency, and SCSp profit distributions to partners are freely remittable without statutory withholding at the partnership level.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable: Luxembourg imposes neither a statutory surrender timeline nor any mandatory conversion ratio for export proceeds. Receipts in EUR or foreign currency may be held in domestic or offshore accounts without restriction, subject only to EU sanctions screening and the bank's internal compliance review.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Moderately viable as a secondary rail: Luxembourg-licensed EMIs (e-money institutions under PSD2) and pan-EU EMIs such as Wise or Airwallex can support non-EUR receivables and low-ticket licensing payments; however, they have reduced commercial-lending capacity and cannot substitute for a full-service Luxembourg bank in high-value SWIFT settlements, documentary credits, or treasury/hedging products. EMI adoption is therefore confined to overflow routing for sub-USD 10,000 SaaS and anti-cheat subscription fees.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In-person meeting of at least one authorised partner or an appointed senior manager (with corporate authority) is generally required at account opening; most tier-1 Luxembourg banks offer an e-signature and videoconference hybrid after the initial physical interview, but fully remote onboarding remains rare for a newly formed SCSp with non-resident partners. A Luxembourg registered office and an up-to-date RBE filing are mandatory prerequisites.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Pass-through SCSp structure with non-resident GP/LP obscuring ultimate beneficial ownership
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised limited partnership agreement (LPA); certificate of registration from the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS); full ownership chain from GP/LP to ultimate natural persons; verified extract from the Lux RBE (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs); passport copies and recent utility bills of all UBOs.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Digital-intangible revenue from gaming-adjacent middleware flagged as non-standard under the bank's activity-sector filter
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed anti-cheat licensing contracts with game studios/publishers; Stripe payout history and SWIFT credit records; sample pro-forma invoices; technical description of kernel-level integrity products; a third-party opinion (legal or audit) confirming the absence of gambling or unregulated-money-services exposure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Low operational history and projected high-frequency subscription inflows triggering enhanced due diligence
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Management team CVs and references; refined 24-month cash-flow forecast with anticipated transaction velocity and average ticket size; board resolution confirming the purpose of the account and prohibition of crypto-cash equivalents; executed data-processing and cybersecurity certifications aligned with ISO 27001 where published.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Partner capital contributions are routed in EUR via SEPA Credit Transfer (preferred) or, for non-EUR, via SWIFT MT103, with the remittance-information field citing the LPA contribution clause. The Luxembourg receiving bank executes ECB/Eurosystem balance-of-payments reporting (direct investment - equity capital) when thresholds apply. USD capital is converted through a dual-currency account with an FX forward overlay at the executing bank; no CSSF or BCL conversion permit is required.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: EUR disbursements clear through SEPA Instant and SEPA Credit Transfer rails; non-EUR and high-value settlements (above EUR 50,000) use SWIFT MT103 with mandatory BIC and structured remittance data, or a Commercial Letter of Credit (UCP600) where the counterparty requires documentary security. Stripe is retained as an auxiliary card/alternative-payment rail for SaaS licensing under USD 10,000 per transaction within permissible PSD2 business models.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable EUR/USD FX forwards used solely for hedging commercial receivables and licensing fees, available under the bank's ISDA/CLE framework without additional licensing

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on EUR/USD as a permissible treasury derivative when physical settlement is operationally undesirable for non-EUR subsidiary receipts, subject to EMIR transparency obligation
Cross-currency interest-rate swaps (EUR/USD) limited to parallel debt-hedging of a future intercompany loan facility and executed under an ISDA 2002 master agreement

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual beneficial ownership confirmation (RBE annual declaration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within one month after the anniversary of the entity's initial RBE registration; a confirmation must be submitted in every calendar year even if no beneficial ownership change occurred.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance constitutes a criminal offence under Luxembourg AML legislation; fines up to EUR 125,000 and imprisonment in serious or recurring cases, plus administrative enforcement and possible suspension of RCS filings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual register audit and statutory appointment confirmation by the registered agent or corporate secretary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registered office provider / corporate secretarial agent acting under the SCSp general partner's authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: To be completed at least once per calendar year before the RBE anniversary confirmation deadline and within 15 days of any change in partners, managers, registered office, or partnership agreement particulars.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Deficient registers and inaccurate RCS/RBE disclosures can lead to fines, civil non-opposability of corporate acts against third parties, and, after repeated warnings, administrative strike-off from the Luxembourg trade register.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Voluntary or mandatory deposit of annual accounts with RCS when audit or publication applies (e.g., CSSF-regulated AIF or partnership agreement election)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after approval of the annual accounts and no later than seven months after the financial year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing is punishable under the Law of 19 December 2002 with fines up to EUR 10,000, compulsory filing at the expense of the liable managers, and possible deregistration after persistent non-compliance.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An unregulated SCSp is generally not subject to a mandatory independent audit because it has no legal personality and is not obliged to publish annual accounts. A statutory audit becomes compulsory when the SCSp is a CSSF-regulated alternative investment fund, when the partnership agreement mandates a réviseur d'entreprises agréé, or when the entity is grouped with a Luxembourg corporate general partner that itself crosses the Luxembourg large-undertaking thresholds.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP in accordance with the Law of 19 December 2002 and EU Accounting Directive 2013/34/EU; IFRS as adopted by the EU may be voluntarily applied where the partnership agreement or fund documentation requires it.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SCSp must identify every individual who directly or indirectly owns or controls more than 25% of partnership interests or voting rights. Any transfer of a limited or general partnership interest must be entered in the internal register immediately and reported to the RBE register within one month of the change. An annual RBE confirmation is filed even when no ownership change has taken place; the confirmation is completed electronically on the LBR portal and attested by a manager of the general partner.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members / Limited and General Partners
Register of Directors / General Partner and Managers
Minute Book of Partner and Manager Meetings

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 0 - 12,000 depending on structure; USD 5,000 - 12,000 if an independent CSSF-regulated audit is required or voluntarily engaged

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 15% standard IRC rate (FY2025) for taxable partners; SCSp is fiscally transparent and not itself an IRC taxpayer. Combined Luxembourg City statutory burden (IRC 15% + solidarity surcharge 1.05% + municipal business tax 6.75%) = 22.80% before deductibility of municipal business tax (effective ~21.7%).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Partners' CIT reliefs: 100% participation exemption on qualifying dividend/ capital gains (10% / €1.2M participation, 12-month holding and substance conditions); IP Box 80% exemption on net IP income, reducing the effective Luxembourg City rate to ~4.56% for qualifying licence income; unrestricted loss carryforward at partner level; ATAD-compliant interest limitation (30% EBITDA) does not apply to the transparent SCSp itself unless the corporate option is exercised.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited (no statutory cap; offset restricted by anti-abuse rules for change of control/activity)
